title: Implied efforts in exclusive dealings
summary: An implied efforts obligation requires a party to take steps toward the contract’s objective even though the agreement does not state that obligation in an express sentence.
notes:
In Wood, the agent’s exclusive control, the owner’s dependence on a share of revenue, the agent’s business organization, and the accounting provisions supported an obligation to use reasonable efforts. Later, Bloor examines an express best-efforts undertaking to promote a beer brand. The cases require attention to the agreement and its commercial setting. They do not establish that every exclusive relationship demands unlimited spending or maximum possible performance. Explain what efforts the particular contract requires and which facts show compliance or failure.

Wood reads exclusivity, contingent compensation, accounting, and related provisions together to imply reasonable efforts. It does not merely insert a favorable obligation because the agreement seems unfair. The casebook compares the sales provision’s “best efforts” wording to the opinion’s “reasonable efforts,” and points to the separate full contract in SEL. Those differences should remain available for interpretation.
